package_info.package_versions: Affected versions prior to patch for CVE-2023-44487 (exact versions not specified in the report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is vulnerable to a protocol-level flaw (HTTP/2 Rapid Reset, CVE-2023-44487) that allows remote attackers to trigger Denial of Service (DoS) by exploiting insufficient limits on certain HTTP/2 frame types, enabling hyper-volumetric DDoS attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Fails to enforce a sufficient limit on the number of RST_STREAM frames received from clients, allowing rapid transitions between open and closed states for requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allows an unbounded number of reset requests in rapid succession, which can be abused to exhaust server resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP/2 server implementations should enforce limits on the number of concurrent streams and reset frames to prevent resource exhaustion. This code fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve handling occasional RST_STREAM frames for client-initiated cancellations, but not at unbounded rates.
key_indicators: No rate limiting or cap on RST_STREAM frames
Allows rapid open/close transitions of streams

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a large number of HTTP/2 RST_STREAM frames in rapid succession to the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server transitions requests between open and closed states without processing, exhausting connection pool.

attack_chain.action: Server resources are exhausted due to unbounded concurrent connections and state transitions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate users.

behavioral_signatures: Unusually high rate of RST_STREAM frames from a single client or IP
Rapid open/close transitions of HTTP/2 streams
Sudden exhaustion of connection pools or thread pools
file_indicators: No explicit rate limiting logic for RST_STREAM in HTTP/2 frame handling code
network_indicators: Burst traffic patterns with high frequency of HTTP/2 RST_STREAM frames
Multiple incomplete or rapidly reset HTTP/2 streams from the same source
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP/2 traffic for excessive RST_STREAM frames per client or connection. Inspect server logs for rapid stream state transitions and connection pool exhaustion. Review HTTP/2 frame handling code for absence of rate limiting or maximum concurrent stream enforcement.
